content.title: Where to watch the Masters Final Round: Tee times, TV, live streams
content.text: The Masters concludes with the final round today. Find out how to watch for free. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Robert Fenbers, cleveland.comAUGUSTA, Ga. - The 2026 Masters concludes with the final round today – Sunday, April 12 – at Augusta National Golf Club in Augusta, Georgia. Today’s finale is available on multiple streaming services. What time does the Masters start today? The final round of the 2026 Masters begins at 9:30 a.m. Eastern. What is the Masters TV schedule today?Final Round - Sunday, April 12All times Eastern.Start time: 9 a.m. TV: 2-7 p.m. on CBSStreaming: 9 a.m.-6 p.m. on ESPN Streaming and 12-2 p.m. on Paramount Plus and 2-7 p.m. on FuboTV How to watch the Masters for freeFuboTV, which offers a free trial, starts at $73.99. You may cancel before the free trial ends to avoid being charged. If not, you can get $25 off your first month. Fubo includes access to more than 185 sports, entertainment and news channels. You can record games, TV shows, movies and more.Paramount+ lets you watch multiple sports like golf, soccer, UFC and NFL at a significantly lower price than most streaming services. They offer the essential package for $8.99 a month and the premium package for $13.99 a month. In addition to CBS, it also features programming from BET, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon, MTV and more. Take in the ultimate Masters streaming experience with PGA TOUR LIVE on the ESPN app. Catch every swing with the Unlimited Plan for $29.99 per month (or $299.99 for entire year) and the Select Plan for $12.99 per month (or $129.99 for entire year).What is PGA Tour Live? PGA TOUR LIVE expanded through ESPN coverage features over 3,200 new hours of live streaming and multiple live feeds available. The live coverage features over 35 tournaments, including the Masters. What happened in Round 3 of the Masters?The stage is set for a dramatic finish after defending champion Rory McIlroy gave away his historic six-stroke lead, finishing one over par in Round 3. Couple that with a potent -7 showing from 2026 Players Championship winner Cameron Young and we have a -11 under par tie at the top of the leaderboard. Sam Burns sits in third place with -10 under while Shane Lowry is fourth at -9 under. Both of those two golfers shot -4 in Round 3. Scottie Scheffler has surged up the standings to a tie for seventh place after a -7 under performance in Round 3. The two-time Masters Champion is just four strokes behind the leaders.
